## What doing it consciously looks like
Most of this I learned by getting it wrong. A few parts I’m still not sure about.
The first problem is that once I’m bonded, I hear things differently. So before making love I want some idea what I’m actually getting into: jealousy, attraction to other people, stress, old patterns, recent healing, money, what each of us wants from the other when things go bad. I don’t get much from asking for the correct philosophy. Put a real situation around it and ask what you think you’d actually do.
Then quit asking questions for a while. Ten profound conversations in one weekend can make me feel like I know somebody when mostly I know what she says about herself. I need boring time too. If I have a little “wait” feeling, it may be nothing. I still want to know what I was about to ignore before I keep going.
The next problem is one decision dragging the next one with it. Sex happens, so moving in feels natural. Once we live together, staying has practical momentum of its own. I’d rather not move in too fast if I have a choice, and I’d pick a date to check in before we need a crisis to force the conversation. Wanting her romantically also doesn’t answer whether I should have children with her or build my life with her. My brain can turn “I’m taking a chance on her” into “she’s the right person” without much new evidence. Sometimes all that changed is that I got more attached.
Meanwhile I want people around who know us together. My friends hear me first; hers hear her first. Fine. They’re our friends. But if nobody knows both of us, the first serious conflict becomes two teams arguing about two different relationships.
And I keep reparenting and meditating when I’m in love. If I stop because my partner makes me feel okay, then she’s doing part of that job for me whether we say so or not.

## What doing it consciously looks like

Most of this I learned by getting it wrong. A few parts I’m still not sure about.

The first problem is that once I’m bonded, I hear things differently. So before making love I want some idea what I’m actually getting into: jealousy, attraction to other people, stress, old patterns, recent healing, money, what each of us wants from the other when things go bad. I don’t get much from asking for the correct philosophy. Put a real situation around it and ask what you think you’d actually do.

Then quit asking questions for a while. Ten profound conversations in one weekend can make me feel like I know somebody when mostly I know what she says about herself. I need boring time too. If I have a little “wait” feeling, it may be nothing. I still want to know what I was about to ignore before I keep going.

The next problem is one decision dragging the next one with it. Sex happens, so moving in feels natural. Once we live together, staying has practical momentum of its own. I’d rather not move in too fast if I have a choice, and I’d pick a date to check in before we need a crisis to force the conversation. Wanting her romantically also doesn’t answer whether I should have children with her or build my life with her. My brain can turn “I’m taking a chance on her” into “she’s the right person” without much new evidence. Sometimes all that changed is that I got more attached.

Meanwhile I want people around who know us together. My friends hear me first; hers hear her first. Fine. They’re our friends. But if nobody knows both of us, the first serious conflict becomes two teams arguing about two different relationships.

And I keep reparenting and meditating when I’m in love. If I stop because my partner makes me feel okay, then she’s doing part of that job for me whether we say so or not.
